title: VLA-FAIL: Efficient Task Failure Detection for Finetuned Vision-Language-Action Models
action_head: flow/diffusion action expert (features taken at the expert's last layer, evaluated at flow time t=0 with one fixed prior-noise sample)
methods: token-wise last-layer Mahalanobis distance (LLMD) to fine-tuning-data feature statistics, max over action-token positions
action chunk consistency (ACC): velocity-normalized disagreement between overlapping parts of consecutive action chunks, EMA-smoothed
new threshold-free metric AUCPDT (precision vs penalized detection time)
ablations: global vs token-wise statistics, RND/logpZO on the same features, velocity normalization
question: Can failures of flow-matching VLAs be detected early and cheaply without any failure data, using out-of-distribution distance in last-layer action-expert features plus self-consistency of successive action chunks?
key_findings: Neither signal alone is reliable across tasks; their OR-combination (FAIL) is the only method in the top three on nearly all real and simulated tasks, matching or beating baselines that need 32 action samples (ACE, STAC, Diff).
LLMD detects failures earlier (looping retries, 'default' actions inconsistent with the scene); ACC catches jerky, erratic OOD motion (real Blocks and Kitchen, all LIBERO-Plus suites).
Token-wise feature statistics beat a single global mean/covariance, e.g. AUCPDT 0.19 vs 0.24 for X-VLA on Drawer (Table 4); authors suggest features differ by how far ahead the token predicts.
Simple Mahalanobis on the fixed-noise features performs on average on par with RND and logpZO density models on the same features (Table 7).
Velocity normalization matters for ACC in simulation, e.g. AUCPDT 0.38 to 0.28 for X-VLA on LIBERO-Plus Spatial.

LIBERO-Plus averages as extracted from a garbled table (column order inferred): FAIL AUCPR 0.94 / AUCPDT 0.18 for X-VLA and 0.72 / 0.47 for pi0.5, vs ACE (32 samples) 0.82 / 0.20 and 0.73 / 0.43, so on pi0.5 FAIL is roughly tied with the sampling baseline.
Overhead: +2.2% latency for X-VLA (136 to 139 ms) and +1.3% for pi0.5 (77 to 78 ms); one-off feature extraction over fine-tuning data takes about 60-67 min.

benchmarks: real: Blocks, Stack T, Cups, Kitchen, Drawer, Mixer
evidence.scale: about 80 real rollouts per policy per task, detectors evaluated over 3 seeds per rollout; LIBERO-Plus over 3 seeds (threshold-dependent appendix results single seed); 20 calibration rollouts for real-world thresholds
evidence.statistics: yes, partial: 95% confidence intervals on threshold-free metrics; no hypothesis tests
evidence.baselines: ACE (action entropy), STAC, Diff (diffusion loss), each with 32 samples and run on replays because they are not real-time; RND and logpZO on the same features; RAPT in the appendix

causal_validation: None. Pure monitoring; no intervention on features.
closed_loop: Rollouts are real closed-loop executions, but detectors are evaluated passively (sampling baselines on replays). No stopping or recovery experiment.
limitations_stated: LLMD needs access to the fine-tuning data for a preprocessing pass.
ACC requires receding-horizon control with sufficient chunk overlap; does not apply to fully open-loop chunk execution.
Misses failures that are consistent in features and actions (confident stopping, ignoring the instruction); combining with VLM-based semantic detectors could help.
critique: Most mechanistically relevant detail for the review: on flow-matching experts, last-layer features are only usable as a monitoring signal after removing sampling noise (fixed prior noise at t=0) and computing statistics per action-token position; this is a practical recipe other probing papers on pi0-family models should note.
The detector is a novelty score, not a failure model; it explicitly cannot catch semantically wrong but confident behavior, which is the failure class interpretability work most cares about.
Only about 80 real rollouts per task; CIs are across detector seeds on the same rollouts, not across independent rollout sets.
Good evaluation practice: a threshold-free metric that penalizes late detection and avoids arbitrary failure-onset annotation; contrasts with SAFE-style metrics that need time-normalized thresholds.
one_line: A Mahalanobis distance on noise-fixed, per-token last-layer features of the flow-matching action expert, OR-ed with a check that consecutive action chunks agree, detects pi0.5 and X-VLA failures without failure data and at about 2% extra latency, roughly matching 32-sample baselines.
